findings.text: The title ("Rule the altitude of information inside a PR body section") names only the nesting/altitude change. The diff also collapses the severity taxonomy from three tiers to two and removes the escalation rule — a materially separate policy change. The body explains and justifies this (Key changes bullet 3, "three tiers stood behind two behaviours..."), so it is not an unexplained hunk, but a reviewer skimming the title alone would not anticipate a severity-scheme change.

Checklist items 1 and 2 name `git show main:...` as their query. `main`'s tip has moved past this PR's merge base (`b9256e4`) and, for `pr-guidelines.md`, now happens to be byte-identical to this PR's head (a separate, differently-authored PR with the same title already landed on `main`). Re-running the literal query against today's `main` is degenerate — it can't discriminate "untouched" from "identical for an unrelated reason." Re-running the same checks against the merge base instead independently confirms the substance: 45 top-level / 0 nested bullets in `pr-guidelines.md` at the merge base (the largest flat list among the 17 files, matching the count in `git ls-tree -r --name-only <merge-base> -- claude/rules claude/skills`), 37 rule bullets inside the five property sections, and the two "restored" `Grounded` rules preserve their pre-reformat requirement.

The clause-by-clause mapping backing "every clause landing at exactly one destination and none dropped or duplicated" lives at `ikuwowfiles/pr-guidelines-reformat-check.md`, which is gitignored and not present in the fetched PR head — the aggregate counts check out (see Note above), but the full 1:1 mapping itself cannot be inspected from a clone.

findings.text: The diff adds a wholly new rule under `Necessary` — "Name a change in a line and leave its detail to the diff, which the reviewer can open; spelling out what an added rule, definition, or table row says is detail, whether quoted, summarized, or given with its consequence" — that has no precedent in the base version of `pr-guidelines.md` (confirmed against `git show b9256e45:claude/skills/git-workflow/pr-guidelines.md`, which has no equivalent clause anywhere in `Necessary`). The Purpose and Key Changes sections describe the `pr-guidelines.md` edit only as a structural reformat ("converting its rule bullets to a one-sentence top line … and lifting onto that line the requirements that sat behind a thesis sentence") plus five explicitly named rule changes (two new `Decidable` rules, the `Fix`/`Note` severity collapse, three bounded rules, the hard-wrap parser fix). None of the five named items covers this new constraint, so a reviewer relying on Key Changes would reach this hunk unwarned.

The one-line change to `claude/skills/git-workflow/SKILL.md` (`"Must Fix" / "Should Fix"` → `"Fix" items, and the "Note" items worth acting on`) is a mechanical consequence of the severity rename described in Key Changes bullet 3, but it is not itself named, and the base `Scoped` rule in effect for this PR ("leaves no unexplained hunks") has no mechanical-consequence exemption — that exemption is one of the changes this very PR is introducing.

Purpose frames the PR's intent narrowly around the `Decidable` altitude/hierarchy problem; the severity-tier collapse (`Fix`/`Note`) and the bounding of three unrelated rules (`Approaches rejected`, `Scoped` hunks, `Grounded` derivation) are explained individually in Key Changes but are not foreshadowed by Purpose, which states only the altitude problem as the reason for the change.

The Verification section's derivation queries cite `main` as the tree-ish (`git ls-tree -r --name-only main …`, `git show main:…`) while the prose claims the counts hold "at the merge base." I independently reproduced the counts against the actual merge-base commit (`b9256e45`) and got matching results (pr-guidelines.md: 45 top-level bullets, 0 nested, the largest flat list among the 17 files; 37 rule bullets in the five property sections), so the claim is correct as authored — but a query keyed to `main` will silently diverge from "the merge base" once `main` moves past that commit, which is exactly what has since happened in this repository.

`ikuwowfiles/pr-guidelines-reformat-check.md`, cited as the record backing the exhaustive clause-mapping claim, is gitignored and not part of the PR diff. It exists on this machine and its structure and row count (103 table rows) are consistent with the claim, but a full clause-by-clause audit against the claim ("every clause landing at exactly one destination and none dropped or duplicated") is not something a reviewer working from a clone can check.

findings.text: Verification checklist items 1, 2, and 5 name the comparison method (`git show main:...`, "reading each section... filtered") but don't inline the command output the way item 3 does (`diff ... both exit 0`). This is permitted by Grounded's documentation-comparison carve-out, and I independently re-verified the underlying claims against the merge-base commit (see below) and found them accurate, so this is a style observation, not a credibility concern.
The clause-mapping record at `ikuwowfiles/pr-guidelines-reformat-check.md` is gitignored, so its contents can't be checked from a clone (the body says so itself).

walk.Decidable: Purpose states the problem and its cause; Key changes bullets carry the claim at the top level with rationale nested beneath, which is the section's own new rule, and the body follows it.
walk.Grounded: independently re-ran the body's own quantitative claims against the merge-base commit (`b9256e4`) — `grep -c '^- '` over the 17 files under `claude/rules` and `claude/skills` confirms `pr-guidelines.md` had 45 top-level bullets and 0 nested (the largest flat list); of those 45, 5 are the property-intro bullets and 3 are template checklist lines, leaving exactly 37 rule bullets, matching the checklist's "37 rule bullets" claim; the two "restored rule" claims (inclusive evidence reading, primary-source rule as a standalone bullet) also match the merge-base wording verbatim.
walk.Necessary: no diff paraphrase, each bullet states a distinct decision, no repeated facts.
walk.Scoped: all three touched files sit inside the stated intent; the one-line `git-workflow/SKILL.md` wording change (`Must Fix`/`Should Fix` → `Fix`/`Note`) isn't named individually in the body, but it's a mechanical consequence of the severity-scheme rename the body does describe, which Scoped's own revised rule exempts from needing a separate mention.
walk.Conformant: title is a one-line summary, no auto-close keywords, checkbox usage matches the rule (all `- [x]` with evidence), and the hard-wrap parser (re-implemented per `pr-selfcheck/SKILL.md`'s spec, including the file's own new "indented line doesn't itself start with a marker" clause) found zero violations in the body.

import re
lines = open('/tmp/pr370_body.md').read().split('\n')
in_fence = False
fence_marker = None
def is_block_marker(line):
    if re.match(r'^(#|\-|\*|\+|\d+\.|\>|\|)', line):
        return True
    if line.startswith('    '):
        return True
    if line.strip().startswith('```') or line.strip().startswith('~~~'):
        return True
    return False

def is_table_row(line):

    return s.startswith('|') and s.endswith('|')

violations = []
prev_nonempty = None
i = 0
while i < len(lines):
    line = lines[i]
    s = line.strip()
    if s.startswith('```') or s.startswith('~~~'):
        in_fence = not in_fence
        prev_nonempty = None
        i += 1
        continue
    if in_fence:

    if s.startswith('<!--'):

        i += 1
        continue
    if s.startswith('>'):

        i += 1
        continue

        i += 1
